predecessors.name: Halaf culture
predecessors.text: northern Mesopotamia, through the Halaf-Ubaid Transitional period

predecessors.name: Samarra culture
predecessors.text: the middle Tigris around Samarra and Tell es-Sawwan

ledger.x: 6000 BCE: the Ubaid farmers of Eridu and 'Oueili, the first settlers of southern Iraq, open the map.
5500 BCE: the Ubaid spreads over the whole southern alluvium and down the Gulf.
5100 BCE: the northern Ubaid replaces the Halaf.
4800 BCE: the Samarra culture of the middle Tigris ends and its land is Ubaid.
4300 BCE: the north passes to the Late Chalcolithic.
4300 BCE: the middle Tigris around Samarra leaves the Ubaid with the north.
4000 BCE: the Gulf coast (Kuwait, Al Jubayl) leaves the Ubaid with the end of the period.
4000 BCE: the Uruk period begins in the south.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture, not a state: every edge is the spread of ceramic finds, never a frontier; the Gulf shore is the only hard line.
